name: Refugi antiaeri de Flix
story: Flix had a large chemical factory and a river crossing, and was bombed repeatedly. Its inhabitants dug this shelter under the old town. On 25 July 1938 Republican units of the XV Army Corps crossed the Ebro in the Flix–Ascó sector at the start of the offensive. On the night of 15–16 November the last Republican troops withdrew back across the river here, ending the Battle of the Ebro. Opened as a museum in 2008, the shelter is part of the Espais de la Batalla de l'Ebre network.
see: Restored shelter galleries beneath the old town, with an exhibition on the bombing of Flix and civil defence.
